risk_report.rationale: The incident narrative describes a patient experiencing loss of consciousness and requiring emergency resuscitation following an unflagged ventricular tachycardia episode. This represents a serious potential patient-safety risk (severity 3) because it involves a failure or missed detection in a safety-critical function that might have led to serious harm, even if no harm actually occurred. The missing device confidence score log for the episode window is concerning and requires investigation.  The EU MDR mandates requirements for electronic programmable systems (mdr-annexI-sec17.1) including repeatability, reliability, and performance in line with intended use, and appropriate means to mitigate risks from single fault conditions. Furthermore, software development must adhere to a lifecycle incorporating risk management and cybersecurity (mdr-annexI-sec17.2). The incident may trigger obligations under these MDR requirements.  The device's automated nature also necessitates compliance with 21 CFR § 820.10(c) regarding design controls (qmsr-820.10-c-design-development), which references ISO 13485. The lack of a retained confidence log hinders assessment and requires investigation to determine the root cause and prevent recurrence.
